text:
Sam Reinhart moved into second on the Panthers' all-time goals list this week, and he keeps adding to it: goals in three straight games, seven in his last ten, 12 on the season. The man who scored 57 two years ago is still the finisher the Panthers lean on.

His own goals are fair, 12 on 12.9 expected, and he's getting to dangerous ice more often than last season. The warning sign is elsewhere. Florida takes only 47% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, nearly eight points worse than when he sits, and the team has scored almost nine more goals than its chances deserve during his shifts. That cushion usually deflates. Part of the explanation is the job: Evolving-Hockey had his competition in the 97th percentile last season, and most of his value came on the penalty kill.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows why the goals come. He gets 1.8 shots per 60 off passes across the slot or from behind the net, the looks that go in about a quarter of the time. Watch whether the five-on-five play catches up to the scoring.
